title: Land a change under branch protection and CI

scenario.brief:
**The ticket.** `main` is protected: nothing lands without a passing CI check and an approving review. Your small fix needs to go in the right way — not by disabling the rules.

You'll open a pull request and hit two gates: the GitHub Actions check is red, and the branch can't merge without a review. Fix the actual cause of the failing check (read the logs), push again until CI is green, get a review, then merge.

**The point:** branch protection is there to protect `main`. The professional move is to satisfy it, never to route around it.
scenario.whyItMatters: On any serious team, `main` is protected and CI gates merges. Knowing how to read a failing check, fix the root cause, and land a change cleanly under those rules is day-to-day senior-engineer work.

setup: Branch from main (e.g. `fix/ci`), make your change, and open a pull request into main.
The CI check will run. If it's red, open the check's logs, find the real cause, fix it, and push again — repeat until green.
Request review. When a reviewer approves and CI is green, merge.
Press Check my work once it's merged.

objectives.title: Make the CI check pass
hints: Read the failing check's logs — fix the cause, don't silence it.
Push more commits to the same branch; the check re-runs.
Never disable protection to force a merge.

objectives.title: Get an approving review
hints: Address comments by pushing more commits.
Protection requires at least one approval.

objectives.title: Merge the pull request
hints: Only once CI is green and it's approved.
Use the merge button; protection lets it through now.
The branch can be deleted after.

debrief.summary: You landed a change under branch protection the right way: you fixed the failing CI check at its source, earned a review, and merged — without weakening the rules that protect main.
internals: Branch protection is a server-side rule on GitHub: it refuses a merge to main unless the required checks pass and the required reviews exist.
The CI check is a GitHub Actions workflow run; its conclusion (success/failure) is what protection gates on.
Pushing new commits to the PR branch re-triggers the workflow, so the fix and the re-check are one loop.
Nothing merged until both gates were green — the history on main stays trustworthy.

keyCommands.note: Push more commits to the PR branch to re-run CI.
See the status of a PR's checks from the terminal.

commonMistakes: Disabling or bypassing branch protection to force a merge.
Silencing a failing test instead of fixing the cause.
Force-pushing over teammates' commits on a shared branch.
debrief.atWork: This is the normal shape of shipping on a protected repo: open, fix CI, get review, merge. Reviewers and CI are collaborators, not obstacles.
debrief.interview: "CI is failing on your PR and main is protected. What do you do?" Answer: read the logs, fix the root cause, push, get review — never bypass protection.
